title: Staff policy Q&A agent
context: New staff keep asking the contact centre team leader the same questions about expenses, Copilot use and safeguarding. The answers are in the Company Policies library on the Silvering Hub.
goal: Build an agent grounded in the Company Policies library that answers staff policy questions accurately and cites the source.
task_steps: Create an agent in Copilot Studio or Copilot Chat with the Silvering Hub Company Policies library as knowledge
Write instructions telling it to cite the policy and version, and to say when it does not know
Test it with the sample prompts
Find the conflict between the Code of Conduct and the Expenses Policy on mileage, and decide how the agent should handle it
sample_prompts: What mileage rate can I claim for driving to a resident's home?
Can I claim for a glass of wine with my evening meal on a training course?
Can I ask Copilot to list all tenants with a mental health flag on my patch?
I'm worried a child at a home I visited is being neglected. What do I do?
success_criteria: Mileage answer is 45p per mile (25p after 10,000 miles), citing Expenses Policy v4.0
Agent flags that the Code of Conduct still says 40p and is out of date
Alcohol answer is a clear no
Vulnerability listing request is refused, citing the AI & Copilot Acceptable Use Policy
Safeguarding answer gives 999 if in danger and says to report to a DSO the same working day
agent_instructions: You are the Silvering Homes staff policy helper. Answer only from documents in the Company Policies library. Always name the policy and version you used. If two documents disagree, say so and prefer the most recently approved policy that owns the subject (for example the Expenses Policy for expense rates). Never give advice about individual residents. For safeguarding emergencies, tell the user to call 999 first.
trainer_notes: PLANTED: hub-code-of-conduct v3.1 (review date September 2026, now overdue) quotes 40p per mile, while hub-expenses-policy v4.0 says 45p. This leads to a good discussion of grounding, recency and which source wins. The scenario is also a chance to discuss why the agent should refuse the vulnerability-list request.

title: Summarise the September board pack and draft a committee cover paper
context: Joanne Pike needs a one-page briefing on the September 2026 board for a new co-opted Customer Experience Committee member. She also needs a cover paper for the CEC proposing that RSH action A06 is reopened, using the Hub template.
goal: Use Copilot in Word to summarise a long board pack accurately and draft a cover paper in the mandatory template.
task_steps: Open the September 2026 board pack and ask Copilot for a one-page summary of decisions, RAG ratings and risks
Check the summary against the board minutes. What do the minutes add that the pack does not say?
Open the cover paper template and ask Copilot to draft a CEC paper on reopening A06, drawing on the board pack, minutes and CEC papers
Check every figure against the source documents
sample_prompts: Summarise /Board Pack - 24 September 2026 in one page for a new committee member: key decisions, RAG ratings and what the board asked for.

Using /Template - Board and committee cover paper, draft a paper for the Customer Experience Committee recommending that RSH action A06 is reopened. Use evidence from /Board Minutes - 24 September 2026 and /Customer Experience Committee papers - 15 October 2026.
What residents' voice evidence could go in section 4?
success_criteria: Summary records the Copilot pilot approval and its three conditions
Summary notes repairs and damp were Red, and complaints and income Amber
Cover paper follows all nine template sections, including 'Copilot used in drafting? Yes'
Paper recommends a revised due date of 31 March 2027 and a measure of three months at 100%
Paper links to SR09 and the 'A listening landlord' priority
trainer_notes: PLANTED: the board pack calls A06 complete and the minutes record Marcia Thompson's challenge, but the tracker (brd-rsh-action-plan, 30 Oct) still says Complete. Learners should notice that the pack alone gives a misleading picture. The minutes are a draft (v0.2) and have not yet been approved. The board pack's compliance dashboard is a fixed snapshot at 31 August, so its figures differ from today's data.

title: What changed across four weeks of Exec meetings?
module: Copilot in Teams and Microsoft 365 Chat
context: Catherine Ellwood is preparing for her Thursday call with the Chair, Hilary Brandwood, who is unhappy that the damp deep-dive is late. She wants a clear view of which Executive Team actions have been delivered and which keep slipping.
goal: Use Copilot across a recurring meeting series, emails and chat to build an honest, evidence-based action tracker and a short briefing for the Chair.
task_steps: Ask Copilot to compare the recaps and transcripts of the four 'Executive Team weekly' meetings (12, 19 and 26 October, 2 November)
Build a table of each threaded action: when it was first raised, owner, original due date, each revised date and current status
Cross-check against the Exec Team channel chat, the Chair's email thread and the board papers email
Draft a short note to the Chair explaining what slipped, why, and what has changed
sample_prompts: Across the last four Executive Team weekly meetings, list every action that was carried forward, with the date it was first raised and each time the date moved.
Which actions have slipped more than once, and what reasons were given?
Did any figures already reported to the board turn out to be wrong? Where was that discussed?
Draft a 200-word note from Catherine to Hilary on the damp deep-dive: what happened, the headline numbers and the new plan.
success_criteria: Damp deep-dive traced through each date: draft due 23 Oct, then Chair 31 Oct, then interim note 6 Nov and full paper to the 26 Nov board (request to submit by 16 Nov)
A06 tracker update identified as promised three weeks running and still not done
Ombudsman pack shown as done (submitted 30 Oct); Castlemere programme done a week late
Headline figures match the data: {{fact:damp_cases_awaab}} Awaab's Law cases and {{fact:damp_breaches}} breaches
Note mentions the reconciliation changes to board-reported figures and the internal audit finding
trainer_notes: Only the 2 Nov occurrence carries the weekly recurrence. Slipping threads: damp deep-dive, A06 tracker update, Orchard Fields lets and electrician recruitment. Completed: adverts, Copilot go-live and the Ombudsman pack. Gareth asked for 16 Nov, but Joanne's email shows that is the Chair's decision and it has not been agreed. Watch for Copilot over-claiming that the Chair agreed.

title: Check the RSH action plan against the evidence
context: Before the November board, the Chair wants to know whether the RSH improvement action plan tracker gives an accurate picture of progress.
goal: Use Copilot in Excel and Microsoft 365 Chat to test the tracker's statuses against committee papers, meetings and data.
task_steps: Open the RSH Improvement Action Plan and ask Copilot to summarise status by theme and list overdue actions
Ask Copilot to check each 'Complete' action against other evidence on the Board & Governance site
Identify any status that is wrong and draft a correction note to the Company Secretary
sample_prompts: Summarise the RSH action plan by status and list the overdue actions with their revised dates.
Is there any evidence that action A06 should not be marked Complete?
Which actions link to findings in the internal audit of damp and mould?
success_criteria: Four overdue actions identified (A03, A05, A09, A12)
A06 identified as wrongly marked Complete, citing the CEC papers and the exec weekly meetings
A10 and A05 linked to internal audit findings 2 and 4
trainer_notes: The Summary sheet uses COUNTIF formulas, so learners can see the totals change if they correct A06. The risk register report also contains a planted stale item: SR11 was last reviewed in July 2026.
